1.explanation:
1. Toggle (in Toggle.js) needs a new `readOnly` prop, corresponding CSS class (`--toggle--readonly`), and an `aria-readonly` attribute on the button so screen readers announce it.  
2. handleClick (inside Toggle.js) must early-exit when `readOnly` is true to prevent state changes and onClick/onToggle callbacks.  
3. Toggle.stories.js must expose the new `readOnly` control in Playground.argTypes, add a default read-only story, and include read-only in the default export so designers and users can see and copy-paste that usage.  
4. Toggle-test.js needs new RTL tests to assert that when `readOnly` is supplied: the button has the read-only class, has the correct `aria-readonly` attribute, and that user clicks do not fire onToggle/onClick callbacks.
1.bug_scenario: The images show the design spec for a new "read-only" appearance of the Toggle component in both small and large sizes: color tokens, typography tokens, spacing measurements, and structural layout for the read-only state (which should look identical to an enabled toggle but not be interactive). They also call out that a read-only toggle must still be announced by screen readers, despite not allowing any value changes.

2.explanation:
• Toggle.js//Toggle: the core component needs a new "readOnly" prop (with PropTypes), styling via classNames, and to propagate aria-readonly to the underlying button.
• Toggle.js//handleClick: must early-return when readOnly is true so that clicking does not change checked state.
• Toggle.stories.js//Playground: the story must expose the new readOnly argType and show a default story for easy copy/paste.
• Toggle-test.js//describe('Toggle'): tests must be added to verify that when the readOnly prop is set (and not disabled), the toggle gets the proper CSS class, has aria-readonly, and does not change state on click while still being announced by screen readers.
2.bug_scenario: The design comps show that the Toggle component must support a new "read-only" state: visually styled like a normal toggle, it remains interactive for screen readers (i.e. announces its value), but does not allow the user to change its state. There are both small and large variants with consistent spacing and color tokens for the read-only appearance.
